newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX natgas futures end off sharply on weather.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX natgas futures end off sharply on weather.

text.p: NYMEX Henry Hub natgas futures ended lower across the board Monday in a sluggish, pre-holiday session, with February again pummeled by technical selling and forecasts for much milder U.S. weather this week, sources said.
February tumbled 30.7 cents to close at $2.677 per million British thermal units. March settled 26.9 cents lower at $2.411. Other deferreds ended down by three to 17.4 cents.

"Technically, it looks pretty bad, but there's some congestion in the $2.50s and $2.60s (basis February) that could offer some support," said one East Coast trader, noting there was not much on the horizon to cheer the bulls.

While technical traders said February could bounce Tuesday ahead of the New Year's Day holiday after a 28 percent dive in three sessions, few expected any upside move to be sustained, with above-normal U.S. weather forecast for the next week and the overall storage gap likely to close further with this week's AGA report.
AGA said its weekly gas storage report will be delayed one day until Thursday due to the holiday.

Chartists pegged near-support in February in the $2.60 area and then at $2.275, a low from November 5. Resistance was seen in today's gap at $2.82-2.96, with selling likely ahead of last Thursday's gap at $3.595-3.61 and then at the contract high of $4.02.

In the cash, January Gulf Coast prices were thinly talked Monday due to the holiday but notionally down about 20 cents to the $2.90s or lower. January Midcon pipes notionally were off 30-40 cents to the low-$3.00 area. January gas at the New York city gate tumbled more than 50 cents to about the $3.45-3.50 level.
The 12-month Henry Hub strip skidded another 11.1 cents to $2.174. NYMEX said 31,824 contracts traded, up from Friday's revised tally of 24,084.
NYMEX Alberta and Permian natgas futures did not trade Monday.
NYMEX will close Tuesday at 1300 EST instead of the usual 1510 EST. The exchange will remain closed Wednesday for the New Year's Day holiday.

On the KCBT, February closed down 32.5 cents at $2.465, while deferreds finished two to 28 cents lower. The East/West spread widened by 1.8 cents to 21.2 cents (NYMEX premium). KCBT said 32 lots traded, down from Friday's 85.
